1

Details

Reach = the X17/IPC(E1) ratio a 50-day run detects at 3σ (Asimov over m_ee histograms in each time-of-flight E_n bin). Only E_n 0.2–2.75 MeV carry X17 here (E* ≤ 22.1 MeV, the ATOMKI-like excitation); the trigger is gated to those arrival times. With X17/IPC constant at all E* the best analysis is the same one (the gate keeps DREAM alive): 8.4×10⁻⁴.

The beam is used in full: 3.7e+08 n/s through the spot, 556 singles per arm per second (time-averaged), DREAM 0.98 live. The reach sits on its IPC + cosmic floor (8.0×10⁻⁴).

The survey had WNR at 1.7×10⁻³–8.5×10⁻³ on the 30° path with an estimated spectrum; here the spectrum is LANL's per-angle yield, the singles come from the soft-beam Geant4 run, and the cell sits at the softest, shortest path.

2

Details

LANSCE, Los Alamos National Laboratory (35.87 N, 106.32 W). Target 4: W cylinder 7.5 cm × Ø3 cm in a 4 mm water jacket (Nowicki, Wender & Mocko, Physics Procedia 90 (2017) 374).

Timing (LANL time-of-flight page): macropulses 625 µs at 40 Hz for Target 4 (the linac can do 120 Hz); micropulses < 100 ps, 7×10⁸ protons each, 1.8 µs apart (3.6 or 7.2 µs on request). The LANL page quotes ~1.5 µA and an RF upgrade to ×2.5 (up to 5 µA); older documents quote ~4 µA (100 Hz).

Contacts: LANSCE User Office (lansce-user-office@lanl.gov); P-3 group leader C. Lee; WNR physicists S. Wender, M. Mocko. lansce_wnr/FACILITY.md.

Six flight paths fan out from a bare W target; MX17 would sit on 90L

top view, not to scale; dashed green = what the X17 set-up adds (collimator to Ø8 cm, dump, ToF trigger gate)

3

Details

4FP90L is the softest path and the shortest (7–15 m); it hosts fission chambers and the NIFFTE fission TPC, a detector of comparable size to one MX17 arm. Its collimation, the beam size at 7–10 m and the room around the beam are not public (ask).

The 30° paths (ICE House ~20 m, ICE-II ~10 m: placed from their quoted fluxes) are electronics-testing stations booked by industry; 15L hosts Chi-Nu; 60R radiography.

At 90° the beam is 55 % in the window and only 4 % above 45 MeV

LANL’s measured-and-calculated yield per proton vs angle (Nowicki 2017 Fig. 2, digitised), at 1.56 µA, 10 m, Ø8 cm

15°

30°

60°

90°

The evaporation peak (0.1–3 MeV) is almost isotropic; the cascade tail is forward.

So the soft flux barely depends on the path, but the hard tail does: ×8 fewer neutrons above 45 MeV at 90° than at 15°.

Cross-check: at 30°, 20 m the curve gives 1.2×10⁶ n/cm²/s above 1.5 MeV; LANL quotes 1.5×10⁶ for ICE House.

4

Details

Y(E) in n/proton/MeV/sr read off Fig. 2 at 20 energies per angle (±10 %). Below 0.1 MeV (no data) Y ∝ √E is assumed; it only feeds wrap-around and singles.

Through the Ø8 cm spot at 10 m and 1.56 µA: ~3.7×10⁸ n/s at 90°, the same as all of NFS, but 55 % of it in the window against NFS's 2 %.

Time of flight does the work: the window is clean of the fast neutrons

top: the beam at the cell; bottom: Geant4 singles per arm within one period (purple: 0.2–2.75 MeV, grey: faster bins)

5

Details

At 10 m the 0.2 MeV neutrons arrive at 1.62 µs, before the next γ flash at 1.83 µs: no frame overlap in the window (wrap-around energy 0.16 MeV, as LANL's table gives). Beyond ~11 m the slowest bin starts to lose its low end to the next frame; 3.6 µs spacing fixes that but halves the protons.

Trigger gate: two-arm triggers accepted only in the purple windows (LANSCE provides the micropulse timing). Inside the gate: 42 random + 0.30 correlated triggers/s, DREAM 0.98 live (non-paralysable, 298 µs, triggers bunched in the 625 µs macropulses).

The singles come from Geant4 (N5 soft forced run below 8.5 MeV, the NFS N4 forced run up to 45 MeV, the 25–45 MeV value above). Prompt ones (within 100 ns of the neutron) fold into the period by their neutron's arrival; delayed ones are flat. Micromegas occupancy (1 µs memory) 0.040.

Distance decides; the angle matters less. Best near 10 m, 1.8 µs

50 days, E* ≤ 22 MeV, big plastics, best throttle; the window is cut at the next γ flash

15°

30°

60°

90°

3.6 µs spacing

Statistics-limited everywhere beyond ~10 m: flux ∝ 1/L².

Closer than 10 m the random two-arm triggers from capture γ bunch inside the macropulses and DREAM goes dead: the beam must be throttled.

At equal distance (15 m) 90° beats 15° by ×1.3: more soft neutrons, fewer hard ones.

3.6 µs halves the protons; 1.8 µs already has no frame overlap below ~11 m.

6

Details

The real paths: 90L at 7–15 m (9.1×10⁻⁴ at 7 m, 8.4×10⁻⁴ at 10 m, 1.3×10⁻³ at 15 m); ICE-II (30R, ~10 m) 1.0×10⁻³; ICE House (30L, ~20 m) 2.2×10⁻³; 15L at 22 m 2.9×10⁻³.

As built, the reach is statistics-limited even at 7 m (1.6×10⁻³): its smaller plastics make fewer trigger legs.

Accidentals and the correlated beam term are ×100 below the IPC: the macropulse duty and the ToF window put the fast neutrons elsewhere in time.

Cosmics are as many as the IPC but sit at m_ee ≈ W (back to back): 1-2 % of them fall in 14-19 MeV, against 36 % of the IPC. a veto leaving 10 % gains only 1 %.

7

Details

The fit uses the m_ee histogram in each time-of-flight bin (W known from E_n). X17 at the ATOMKI ratio is 0.7 % of the IPC after cuts.

Exposure per bin = DREAM live 0.98 × exp(−2 × Micromegas occupancy). Accidentals: the pairing integral of the singles' time profile over each bin, ×2δ (δ = 5 ns), scaled to the NFS histogram of that bin by the same integral for NFS's own beam (so the NFS vertex + E_sum pass fraction is used).

Same apparatus, same cuts, same fit: only the beam changes.

WNR is the only white pulsed source that passes ATOMKI: its micropulses spread the beam over 13 889 bursts a second, and time of flight throws the fast neutrons away.

Unlike MEDAPP (reactor off) and Birmingham (no port), it runs today with a flight path built for TPC-sized detectors.

Details

Reference rows: ILL PF1B 5.3×10⁻³; GANIL NFS 1.6×10⁻²; n_TOF EAR2 1.2×10⁻¹ (survey_fast.py); FRM II MEDAPP and Birmingham from survey/soft_sim/soft_reach.py. WNR at 100 Hz (×2.5 current, the LANL upgrade): 5.5×10⁻⁴, 6.6 d to ATOMKI.

What moves it: the IPC shape, not the beam model

S/B ≈ 0.7 %: an uncorrelated 2 % shape error per m_ee bin costs ×1.4. The IPC m_ee shape must be known (or fitted from the fast bins).

The > 45 MeV neutrons (4 % at 90°) have no Geant4 behind them; scaling their response ×10 moves the reach little, because time of flight puts them outside the window.

9

Details

K_HI: singles, legs, triggers and correlated pairs per neutron above 45 MeV, as a multiple of the 25–45 MeV values (N4). δ: an uncorrelated relative uncertainty on the background in every m_ee bin (nfs_reach.z2_asimov's δ term). lansce_wnr/out/wnr_khi_sensitivity.csv.

What this does not settle yet

Not in the simulation

• The γ flash in the Micromegas (1 µs drift) at the start of the window.

• The flight-path room, the collimator and the dump: re-weighted from the NFS geometry (vacuum tube, no hall).

• Neutrons above 45 MeV: response extrapolated (×0–10 checked).

Facility

• 90L beam time is scarce; the ICE paths are booked by industry.

• The spectrum is digitised by eye from one figure (±10 %).

• X17/IPC for E1 capture at E* 20.6–22 MeV vs ATOMKI’s p + t: the physics question under every neutron number.
